content: 1. Clarithromycin increases the levels of bosutinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of brigatinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by approximately 50% (e.g., from 180 mg to 90 mg or from 90 mg to 60 mg). After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor, resume the previously tolerated brigatinib dose. 3. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Clarithromycin raises the levels or effects of budesonide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and buprenorphine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Clarithromycin and buprenorphine (buccal, subdermal implant, or transdermal) both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buspirone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Butabarbital reduces the levels or effects of vonoprazan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, reduce the cabazitaxel dose (e.g., by 40 mg/day for Cometriq or 20 mg/day for Cabometyx). Resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 10. Clarithromycin increases the levels of cabergoline by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of cabozantinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is required, reduce the cabozantinib dose (e.g., by 40 mg/day for Cometriq or 20 mg/day for Cabometyx). Resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 12. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of calcitriol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Clarithromycin raises the levels or effects of capivasertib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 14. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of vonoprazan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor plasma levels if used concomitantly. 15. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ceritinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Both ceritinib and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of chloroquine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Chlorpromazine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Clarithromycin and cholera vaccine exhibit pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Clarithromycin raises the levels or effects of cinacalcet by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Clarithromycin and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Clarithromycin and citalopram both increase the risk of QTc prolongation and toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for QT interval prolongation or ventricular tachyarrhythmias if coadministered. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clomipramine and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Clarithromycin reduces the levels or effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which reduces clopidogrel bioactivation. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of clozapine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and clozapine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Clarithromycin and cobicistat both increase each other's levels by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of colchicine by affecting P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Use of colchicine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens (oral or vaginal) by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of copanlisib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cortisone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Clarithromycin and crizotinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of vonoprazan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin increases the levels of dabrafenib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Clarithromycin enhances the effects of dalteparin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Vonoprazan reduces the levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 36. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of daridorexant by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of darifenacin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Clarithromycin and degarelix both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Desflurane and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Desipramine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of diazepam by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Clarithromycin and disopyramide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 46. Clarithromycin and dofetilide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Donepezil and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 48. Doxepin and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 49. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and dronedarone prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 50. Clarithromycin and droperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 51. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the dose to 30 mg orally once daily. For NVAF, no dose reduction is recommended. 52. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of vonoprazan by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Both efavirenz and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 53. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 54. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of vonoprazan by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 55. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 56. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of eletriptan by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Separate administration by 72 hours. 57. Clarithromycin and eliglustat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 58. Clarithromycin increases the levels of eluxadoline by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg orally twice daily. 59. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 60. Encorafenib reduces the levels or effects of vonoprazan by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and encorafenib prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose (e.g., from 450 mg/day to 150 mg/day). Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives. 61. Clarithromycin enhances the effects of enoxaparin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 62. Enzalutamide reduces the levels or effects of vonoprazan by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 63. Clarithromycin and entrectinib both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of entrectinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with entrectinib, a CYP3A4 substrate. Resume the previous entrectinib dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives. 64. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of enzalutamide by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 65. Epinephrine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 66. Racemic epinephrine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 67. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider reducing the dose accordingly. If the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the erdafitinib dose in the absence of drug-related toxicities. 68. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ergoloid mesylates by reducing their metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 69. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ergotamine by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 70. Eribulin and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If concurrent use is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 71. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Vonoprazan reduces the levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 72. Clarithromycin and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 73. Eslicarbazepine acetate reduces the levels or effects of vonoprazan by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 74. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
